headline: On October 9, 1981: Mitterrand abolishes capital punishment
captionCards: First left-wing president under the Fifth Republic
Longest-serving republican head of state in French history
instagramCaption:
François Mitterrand ended the death penalty in France.

The newly elected President signed the abolition law into effect on October 9, 1981. This marked a historic shift as he became the first left-wing politician to assume the presidency under the Fifth Republic. He would go on to remain in office longer than any other republican head of state in French history, serving until 1995.

This decisive action permanently altered the French legal landscape and human rights standards for decades to come.
